result:
Changed the request framing; kept the loose key match underneath.

What changed: the request now reads "Set the 'Login fails on checkout' issue in one of the PAY teams - the private one described as handling checkout billing - to High priority." Condition texts updated to match ("one of the PAY teams" / "described as handling checkout billing" / "the private one"). Seed, query, decoys, and write are untouched.

Why: the reader was right that "with PAY in its key" plus two more technical clauses sounded like a checklist. The new phrasing is how a colleague narrows among several similar-looking teams — and the seed backs it (PAY, PAYB, PAYS, PAYR, plus a "PAY Support" team).

What I kept and why: the key condition still matches loosely (contains PAY) rather than exact "the PAY team". Team.key is unique per organization, so the description/privacy decoys must carry PAY-like keys (PAYB/PAYS/PAYR) to fail only their own fact — an exact-key wording would make them fail the key condition too and break the near-miss design.
